sections.title: F-1: Acronyms
sections.summary: Presents the acronym list used throughout UFC 3-250-04, covering organizations (ACI, ASTM, DoD, USACE, TSC, TSPDWG), concrete/pavement-specific terms (RCC, RCCP, PCC, ASR, w/cm, GGBFS), materials chemistry symbols (Al2O3, CaO, Fe2O3, SiO2), QC/QA terms (CQC, QA, QC, DCP, GPR), and SI/US-customary units of measure used in the tables and text.
sections.body: Appendix F, Section F-1 is an alphabetized acronym list translating each abbreviation used in the body of UFC 3-250-04 to its full term. The list spans several categories: engineering/standards organizations (ACI - American Concrete Institute, ASTM - American Society for Testing and Materials, DoD - Department of Defense, USACE - United States Army Corps of Engineers, TSC - Transportation Systems Center, TSPDWG - Tri-Service Pavement Discipline Working Group, IPRF - Innovative Pavement Research Foundation Report); materials chemistry symbols used in cement/pozzolan/slag chemistry (Al2O3 - Aluminum Oxide, CaO - Calcium Oxide, Fe2O3 - Iron(III) Oxide or Ferric Oxide, SiO2 - Silicon Dioxide (Silica)); concrete- and pavement-specific abbreviations (RCC - Roller-Compacted Concrete, RCCP - Roller-Compacted Concrete Pavement, PCC - Portland Cement Concrete, HMA - Hot Mix Asphalt, GGBFS - Ground-Granulated Blast Furnace Slag, w/cm - Water/Cementitious Material Ratio, LL - Liquid Limit, PI - Plasticity Index, SG - Specific Gravity, TEA - Triethanolamine, ASR - Alkali-Silica Reaction); quality and field-testing abbreviations (CQC - Contractor Quality Control, QA - Quality Assurance, QC - Quality Control, DCP - Dynamic Cone Penetrator, GPR - Ground-Penetrating Radar); document-series abbreviations (UFC - Unified Facilities Criteria, UFGS - Unified Facilities Guide Specification); and a full set of SI and US customary units of measure used throughout the tables and equations of the document (e.g., ft, in., m, m2, mm, mm/m, kPa, MPa, psi, kg/m, kg/m2, kg/m2/hr, kg/m3, lb/ft, lb/ft2, lb/ft2/hr, lb/yd2, oz/yd2, yd2, tsf, gm/m2, mg/m3, Hz, CONUS - Continental United States, FOD - Foreign Object Damage).
key_points: RCC = Roller-Compacted Concrete; RCCP = Roller-Compacted Concrete Pavement -- the subject of Appendix E and used throughout the document.
PCC = Portland Cement Concrete; w/cm = Water/Cementitious Material Ratio -- key mixture-design terms.
ASR = Alkali-Silica Reaction, a deleterious chemical reaction addressed in materials selection and defined in the glossary (F-2).
GGBFS = Ground-Granulated Blast Furnace Slag, a supplementary cementitious material.
CQC = Contractor Quality Control; QA = Quality Assurance; QC = Quality Control -- core RCC construction QC/QA terms.
DoD = Department of Defense; USACE = United States Army Corps of Engineers; TSC = Transportation Systems Center; TSPDWG = Tri-Service Pavement Discipline Working Group.
UFC = Unified Facilities Criteria; UFGS = Unified Facilities Guide Specification -- the document series this manual belongs to.
HMA = Hot Mix Asphalt, referenced throughout for RCC paving/compaction technique comparisons.
DCP = Dynamic Cone Penetrator; GPR = Ground-Penetrating Radar -- field testing/investigation acronyms.
ACI = American Concrete Institute; ASTM = American Society for Testing and Materials -- standards-writing bodies cited throughout Appendix G.
Materials chemistry symbols used for cement/slag/pozzolan chemistry: Al2O3, CaO, Fe2O3, SiO2.
The list also includes a full set of SI and US customary measurement-unit abbreviations (e.g., kPa, MPa, psi, kg/m3, lb/ft2, tsf) used throughout the document's tables and text.
sections.applicability: Applies as a reference key for interpreting acronyms used throughout UFC 3-250-04, including Appendix E (RCC pavements).

sections.title: F-2: Definition of Terms
sections.summary: Defines 16 technical terms used throughout the document relating to concrete materials, properties, and pavement construction practice, including alkali-silica reaction, compaction, curing, strength definitions, supplementary cementitious materials (fly ash, GGBFS, pozzolan, silica fume), aggregate grading, and joint-related hardware/defects (dowels, tie-bars, D-cracking, slipform paving).
sections.body: Appendix F, Section F-2 defines 16 technical terms used elsewhere in UFC 3-250-04. Alkali-Silica Reaction (ASR) is a chemical reaction between alkalis in cement and certain reactive silica minerals in aggregate that forms a gel, which absorbs water and expands, damaging the concrete. Compaction is the process of reducing void volume by applying mechanical energy. Compressive Strength is the maximum resistance of a concrete specimen to axial compressive loading. Curing is maintaining moisture and temperature conditions in a freshly placed cementitious mixture to allow cement hydration to occur. Dowels are round steel bars that extend into adjoining slabs at an expansion or contraction joint to transfer shear loads. D-Cracking is a pattern of cracks formed parallel to a joint or linear crack due to the inability of the concrete to withstand environmental factors such as freeze-thaw cycles. Durability is the ability of concrete to resist weathering action, chemical attack, and abrasion. Flexural Strength is the maximum resistance of a concrete specimen to flexural loading. Fly Ash is a fine powder byproduct of burning pulverized coal in electric power generating plants, used as a supplementary cementitious material. Gap-Graded Aggregate is an aggregate graded so that one or more intermediate-size fractions are absent. Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag (GGBFS) is a granular byproduct of the iron- and steel-making process, dried and ground into a fine powder, highly cementitious and high in calcium silicate hydrates. Pozzolan is a siliceous or siliceous-and-aluminous material that in itself possesses little or no cementitious value, but in finely divided form and in the presence of moisture, chemically reacts with calcium hydroxide to form compounds having cementitious properties. Silica Fume is a byproduct of producing silicon metal or ferrosilicon alloys and a very reactive pozzolan. Slump is a measure of the consistency of freshly mixed concrete, equal to the subsidence of a molded specimen immediately after removal of the slump cone. Slipform Paver is a paver that does not use fixed forms but has forms that are pulled or raised as concrete is placed. Tie-Bar refers to deformed steel bars or connectors used to hold the faces of abutting slabs in contact, typically used at longitudinal joints.
key_points: Alkali-Silica Reaction (ASR): a chemical reaction between cement alkalis and certain reactive silica minerals in aggregate that forms an expansive gel, damaging concrete as it absorbs water and expands.
Compaction: the process of reducing void volume in fresh concrete by applying mechanical energy.
Curing: maintaining moisture and temperature conditions in a freshly placed cementitious mixture to allow cement hydration to occur.
Dowels: round steel bars extending into adjoining slabs at an expansion or contraction joint to transfer shear loads.
D-Cracking: a pattern of cracks forming parallel to a joint or linear crack, caused by concrete's inability to withstand environmental factors such as freeze-thaw cycles.
Fly Ash: fine powder byproduct of burning pulverized coal in power plants, used as a supplementary cementitious material.
Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag (GGBFS): a dried, finely ground granular byproduct of iron/steel-making, highly cementitious and high in calcium silicate hydrates.
Pozzolan: a siliceous (or siliceous and aluminous) material with little cementitious value alone, but which reacts with calcium hydroxide in the presence of moisture to form cementitious compounds.
Silica Fume: a byproduct of producing silicon metal or ferrosilicon alloys; a very reactive pozzolan.
Slump: a measure of freshly mixed concrete consistency, equal to the subsidence of a molded specimen after removing the slump cone.
Slipform Paver: a paver that uses no fixed forms; its forms are pulled or raised as concrete is placed.
Tie-Bar: deformed steel bars or connectors that hold the faces of abutting slabs in contact, typically at longitudinal joints.
sections.applicability: Applies as the defined-terms reference for concrete materials, properties, and pavement construction terminology used throughout UFC 3-250-04.
